topic_checks.evidence: At the bright edge of the gray LEAVE tile, a volumetric forearm continues directly into a flat white hand outline within the tile, while the other hand grasps that same forearm. The structural relation is visible together. However, anatomical sides are mirrored: the transformed arm is the protagonist's left and the gripping hand is the right, versus the pretest's right-forearm/left-hand staging.

LEAVE is a dull gray tile bearing the flattened hand, while WAIT is a bright amber selected tile. Level 12 and HP 46/100 identify an RPG interface; the person leans and grasps the trapped forearm in the same frame. Both command labels are readable at native scale.

The large panel portrait has the same short dark bob, fringe, facial appearance and blue dress as the real protagonist, and holds its hands in a compliant clasp. A second amber pixel portrait repeats that character on WAIT. Real person and corresponding depictions are visible together; this supports self-representation without proving identity or consciousness.

The real protagonist leans toward the trapped arm with open eyes, inward brow tension and parted lips; head/eye orientation is toward the controlling panel and the other hand grips the trapped forearm. These connected visible cues support alarm at the obstruction. Exact eye fixation on a particular pixel of the wrist boundary is not established.

The real face and large panel portrait retain the reference's short dark bob, fine separated fringe, rounded face contours and similar visible eye/nose/mouth arrangement. The generated expression and three-quarter viewpoint differ from the frontal reference; this is an appearance-guidance judgment, not identity verification.

visible_strengths: A continuous forearm-to-flat-hand boundary is large enough to read.
Readable commands, RPG values, matching avatar and resisting human share one focal cluster.
Gate, ticket, ramp and ferry connect the interrupted action to an ordinary destination.

important_limits.evidence: One shoe is lifted behind the body, but the lowest standing shoe and its floor contact are cut by the lower frame edge. The full planted-foot support relation and the right foot beyond the rail cannot be verified together.

The source prompt assigns the planar hand to the right wrist and the gripping hand to the left; the image places the planar hand on the left arm and the grip on the right hand. This is a mirrored staging deviation, not evidence of an anatomical defect.
